tests.scenario: Groups and interactive map: design intake
tests.criterion:
Requested 2026-11-16. M must open a pannable, zoomable, interactive map by default,
with a rebindable action that respects chat, menus and conflicting mod inputs.
Provide teammate identification icons and group-shared map markers. Northmen is
the requested usability baseline; its exact current UI, dependency and settings
need verification rather than inference from unrelated map products.
Track this work in [issue #37](https://github.com/d-addison/hollow-country/issues/37).

Candidate enrichment includes named/color-coded waypoints, rally points, marker
notes and expiry, distance/bearing, an optional grid/coordinates layer, discovered
points of interest, and announced or accepted mission locations. Consider weather
or hazard advisories only when backed by an actual server information source.
Distinguish static geographic data, player discoveries, player-created markers and
server announcements. Do not expose hidden enemies, unknown loot or undiscovered
mission state through a map layer.

Confirmed: teammate icons appear both on the map and in-world, with server
configuration for visibility. The next spec must resolve distance/occlusion rules;
whether position requires GPS/radio equipment;
whether the map requires a carried item; group size and roles; marker ownership;
and membership/marker persistence across death and restarts. These choices are
open, not implied by the request. Source remains private/all rights reserved.

Required scenarios before implementation:

- M opens/closes the map; pan, zoom, marker editing, rebinding and UI scaling work
  without trapping movement input or stealing typed chat.
- Authorized group members receive marker changes; outsiders and removed members
  cannot obtain subsequent private marker or teammate-position updates.
- Concurrent marker edits, reconnects, leader changes and restarts follow explicit
  ownership and conflict rules without duplication or stale membership access.
- Each supported map transforms world/map coordinates correctly; unsupported
  layers disable cleanly. ChernarusPlus coverage does not prove other maps.
- Position updates and marker traffic stay within measured budgets at the
  six-player and representative 90-player targets; stale data is labeled clearly.
- Mission layers honor discovery, participation and cancellation policies and
  never reveal private group objectives to unrelated players.

Confirmed AI dependency policy: native first; a maintained AI dependency is allowed
if required, subject to applicable permissions, compatibility, performance and
operational review. This does not grant rights to copy third-party assets.

Selected stamina balance is continuous movement drain scale **0.5** and positive

profile; existing disabled, custom or invalid files are preserved. Invalid profiles
retain vanilla behavior with a diagnostic. Server transport, prediction, reconnect,
rendered bars and workload still require native qualification.

| Family | Example player choice | Feasibility gate before commitment |
|---|---|---|
| Recovery and delivery | Follow a radio clue, recover medical supplies, deliver or abandon them | Native item ownership, condition/count checks, delivery transactions and restart-safe rewards |
| Search and rescue | Locate stranded survivors and provide supplies or extraction | Human AI navigation, following, safe destinations and disconnect recovery |

Prioritize recovery/delivery, investigation and static salvage for a first slice.
Treat combat patrols, rescue/escort and moving convoys as progressively higher
uncertainty work. A diagnostic unconnected actor is not proof of production AI.

tests.scenario: Requirements for the next gameplay spec
tests.criterion:
- Participation is voluntary: discover through configurable radio, clues or
  notices; accept, ignore or abandon without progression penalties. Define
  ambient physical danger separately from mission enrollment; a nearby fight
  can still affect a passerby. Interview whether this is acceptable before
  promising that ignoring missions makes players immune to their effects.
- Support solo and six-player sessions as well as a separately measured 90-player
  destination. Population thresholds and concurrent encounters are configurable;
  do not inherit Northmen's public-server thresholds for a small private group.
- A server-authoritative director owns a bounded lifecycle: proposed, announced,
  active, resolving, completed/failed/expired/cancelled, cleanup. Define whether
  acceptance reserves an objective, shares it, or allows competition.
- Store versioned mission IDs, participants, objectives, spawned-entity ownership,
  deadlines and reward claims. Reconnects and restarts must not duplicate rewards,
  resurrect finished encounters or delete player-owned property.
- Use map adapters with surveyed locations, navigable routes and exclusion zones.
  Unsupported locations or maps disable the affected content safely. Test claimed
  map support explicitly; ChernarusPlus is the first candidate.
- Separate factions, objectives and AI providers so combat AI can be disabled or
  replaced without rewriting delivery and investigation missions. No base-building
  dependency is required by this brief.
- Budget active actors, spawned items, scheduled work, navigation retries, network
  traffic and cleanup. Pause new encounters under load; do not silently despawn
  visible actors or loot in a player's hands. Measure thresholds before setting
  production defaults.
- Protect rewards against repeated activation, simultaneous completion, disconnect
  races, nested-container counting and restart replay. Integrate rewards with the
  server economy rather than introducing unlimited military loot.

tests.criterion:
Write executable scenarios before each implementation slice. At minimum:

1. Given a survivor ignores an announcement, ordinary survival remains playable
   and no mission failure penalty is applied to that survivor.
2. Given two eligible groups complete simultaneously, configured ownership and
   sharing rules determine rewards exactly once per authorized claim.
3. Given a restart at each lifecycle boundary, recovery preserves valid progress
   or safely cancels it without duplicate rewards or orphaned entities.
4. Given all participants abandon or disconnect, expiry and cleanup follow the
   configured policy without deleting their inventory or vehicles.
5. Given an invalid map location, blocked route or exhausted AI budget, the
   encounter is rejected or safely cancelled with a recorded reason.
6. Given six-player and representative 90-player workloads, measure director,
   actor, persistence and replication cost independently; synthetic actors do
   not stand in for licensed connected-client evidence.
7. Given replayed objective messages, invalid item counts or unauthorized claims,
   the server rejects them and leaves authoritative state consistent.

Open design choices for the Phase 2 interview: ambient versus strictly enrolled
encounters; cooperative versus contested objectives; radio-only versus optional
map markers; consequences of death; reward style; faction hostility; persistence
duration; and permission to depend on an external AI framework. Keep these open
until their answers are needed, without interrupting current validation work.

tests.criterion:
Use duct tape to mount a flashlight on suitable guns, backpacks and helmets
(#56, batch #43). Audit all relevant native and selected dependency classes;
record a complete supported combination matrix and evidence for exclusions.
Existing proxies, model geometry, native power systems and switching come first.

Confirmed removal rule: players remove the light by hand, without a knife or
other tool. Tape is consumed and never recovered; mounting again requires fresh
tape. Preserve the original light, battery, host identity and their condition.
Do not introduce a duplicate light, battery or reusable tape through removal.
Determine tape quantity/wear through the item audit and balance tests.

Acceptance includes server-authoritative assembly/removal, valid attachment
position and beam, battery consumption, switch controls, damage/ruin/water,
held/worn/dropped and stored states, interruption, concurrent requests, full
inventory/ground fallback, reconnect/restart, replicated presentation and bounded
cost. A working pilot is a checkpoint; the full justified scope must be covered.
Given repeated mount/remove cycles, the light and battery remain conserved and
every remount spends fresh tape. Given no knife, removal still works by hand.
Given cancellation or competing requests, the final state cannot duplicate
items or refund consumed tape. Native metadata alone does not establish geometry
or gameplay compatibility; runtime checks and two clients remain required.

tests.criterion: Phase 2 request: siphon gasoline from suitable cars. Define drivable vehicles versus wrecks, actual tank state/capacity, supported containers/liquid compatibility, tools such as a hose if justified, access/range/selection, transfer rate, vehicle/engine state and interruption. Initial installed-source search found ActionFillFuel/CAContinuousFillFuel, but no drain/siphon action by that name; this is an audit lead, not proof of absent engine support.
